transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-12-11
Time: 10:00 AM PT
Duration: ~50 minutes
Attendees: Maya Henderson (Redwood AE), Ethan Park (Redwood SE), Riley Kim (Redwood SE), Laura Chen (Enterprise Services Head of IT), Raj Patel (CISO), Sofia Gomez (Identity Engineer), Tom Rivers (Cloud Ops)

Auto-summary (auto-generated, might be rough): Reviewing SSO/SAML configuration, SCIM provisioning for users/groups, RBAC least-privilege approach. Customer asks about audit logs, retention, encryption and KMS, and private/VPC options for data residency. Next steps and artifacts to be shared.

Transcript body:
[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. We're here to walk through SSO and SCIM and how Redwood maps to your RBAC model. Quick intros?
[00:08] Laura: Hi this is Laura, head of IT at Enterprise Services.
[00:10] Raj: Raj Patel, CISO, quick thanks for doing this.
[00:12] Sofia: Sofia, identity engineer, I'll own SCIM work on our side.
[00:16] Tom: Tom Rivers, cloud ops, I'll handle networking questions.
[00:20] Maya: Awesome. Ethan and Riley from our SE team — Ethan will go deep on SCIM mappings and RBAC. Riley will cover audit logs and KMS.
[00:28] Ethan: Cool, I'll start with SAML SSO overview. Redwood supports SAML 2.0 and OIDC, we commonly do a SAML IdP integration for enterprise SSO. You can map attributes like email, name, and groups. We can do group claim mapping or SCIM for provisioning.
[00:42] Raj: On the SAML side, we need to know about SP-initiated vs IdP-initiated flows, metadata exchange, and certificate rotation. Also MFA enforcement — does Redwood honor the IdP enforced MFA?
[00:55] Ethan: Yes, we support both flows. SP/IdP initiated both supported. We surface the metadata XML and assertion consumer URL in the console. For certificate rotation we have a rotation window and notify customers; we also support metadata signing validation. MFA is enforced at IdP level — Redwood trusts the IdP assertion, we do not re-prompt.
[01:12] Sofia: For SCIM, do you support SCIM 2.0 and which attributes? We need group membership sync and department attributes — mapping to RBAC roles.
[01:21] Riley: We support SCIM 2.0; common attributes include userName, displayName, emails, groups, externalId. We can do group-to-role mappings — for example, map SCIM group 'redwood-admins' to role Admin in Redwood. We can provide examples of mapping rules.
[01:36] Sofia: Also need to know behaviour on user deprovisioning — if user removed from IdP, do we immediately revoke tokens or is there TTL?
[01:45] Ethan: Good question. Our default behavior is immediate deprovisioning on SCIM deletion: we set user to disabled and revoke active API tokens. We have configurable grace periods for some flows but prod recommended is immediate revocation for security-sensitive customers.
[01:58] Tom: On the network side, if we go private or VPC peering, how does SAML traffic work? Are assertions POSTed through the public control plane or can SAML be routed over private link?
[02:09] Riley: For Redwood Private we run the control plane inside your VPC — SAML metadata and assertion endpoints can be hosted privately. For hosted customers, assertions go to our hosted control plane endpoint over HTTPS; we recommend IdP IP allowlisting if you have strict control. We'll walk through VPC peering options in the follow-up.
[02:26] Raj: Audit logs — we need detailed logs for user activity, admin actions, and provisioning events. Retention needs to be 12 months off-box, and we need export capability to our SIEM.
[02:37] Riley: We emit audit logs for admin actions, API keys, token issuance, SCIM provisioning events, and model route changes. Logs are available in the Console and via pull APIs or log forwarders to your Splunk/Datadog. Retention on hosted plans is 90 days by default, with add-on for 12 months. For Private we can discuss on-prem or customer-managed storage.
[02:55] Laura: Is there a schema for the logs? Need example fields and event ids for compliance review.
[03:01] Riley: We'll share the audit log schema. It includes timestamp, user_id, actor_email, action_type, resource_type, resource_id, request_ip, and outcome. We'll throw an example file in the docs we send.
[03:12] Sofia: KMS integration — do you support customer-managed keys? We want to ensure encryption at rest with our keys, and separation for logs/encryption.
[03:21] Ethan: Yes, Redwood supports CMEK for Private and some Dedicated deployments — integrations with AWS KMS and customer HSMs via our key wrap approach. For hosted plans, we use provider-managed keys by default but can discuss BYOK arrangements for enterprise contracts.
[03:36] Raj: Is there key rotation support and audit trail for key usage? We need proof keys were rotated and access logs for key use.
[03:43] Riley: KMS rotations are reflected in the control plane, and we record key usage events in audit logs. We can produce an attestation summary for key rotation windows.
[03:52] Tom: Data residency — we need data to remain in our EU region. Does Redwood host inference and control plane in region?
[03:59] Ethan: We have regional hosting for both inference and control plane. For EU residency we can pin the workload to eu-west-1 region and ensure logs and payloads are stored in-region. For extra assurance, Private deployment in your VPC is the strongest option.
[04:12] Raj: SOC2 and ISO artifacts — can you share the reports and any gap analysis? Also pen test results?
[04:19] Maya: Yes — we will share SOC2 Type II report summary and ISO27001 certification summary. Pen test reports are available under NDA; we can route those through our security portal. I'll send links after the call.
[04:30] Laura: On RBAC — we have a least-privilege model, many teams, and need nested groups support. How granular can Redwood roles be? API access, console access, model and route level permissions?
[04:42] Ethan: Redwood RBAC supports role-based roles with permissions scoped to resources. You can create roles that allow only embeddings creation, or only model inference, or admin tasks. We support resource-level scoping: per-project or per-route permissions. Nested group support currently via SCIM group mapping; we can map groups into roles and support multiple group claims.
[04:58] Sofia: We want to avoid giving devs access to production models and logs. Can we create environment-based roles?
[05:05] Riley: Yes — create roles per environment and map corresponding SCIM groups. We also support time-limited access tokens and role expiry via SCIM/IdP workflows.
[05:16] Raj: For compliance, we need separation of duties — like a security admin can't modify billing. Is the billing portal separated?
[05:22] Maya: Billing is a separate role and console area. We can gate billing permissions to a finance group and ensure security admins don't get billing access. We'll include recommended role templates in the docs.
[05:33] Laura: Any gotchas around SCIM provisioning of service accounts? We have some machine accounts that need API keys not tied to a person.
[05:40] Ethan: Service principals are supported — you can provision machine users and bind them to roles. API keys for machine accounts are managed similarly and can be rotated automatically by policy. We recommend using short-lived tokens if possible.
[05:54] Sofia: How do you handle orphaned accounts if someone leaves? We want automated flags for inactive accounts after X days.
[06:01] Riley: We support inactivity policies and heartbeat checks; we can flag accounts not seen for 30/60/90 days and optionally disable them automatically. That can be part of your SCIM deprovisioning rules.
[06:10] Tom: Network allowlisting — we need to restrict API calls to our IP ranges. Is that possible for hosted?
[06:16] Maya: Hosted customers can use IP allowlisting on keys and per-project allowlists; Private gives full network controls. We'll provide the IP ranges and recommended configs.
[06:26] Laura: Regarding logs to SIEM, can you confirm the delivery mechanism? Kafka? Kinesis? HTTP?
[06:33] Riley: We have webhooks, S3 export, direct integrations with Datadog and Splunk via HTTP forwarders, and streaming via Kinesis. We'll include the delivery patterns.
[06:44] Raj: Encryption in transit — TLS versions, mTLS support for service-to-service?
[06:49] Ethan: TLS 1.2+ enforced, recommend 1.3. For Private deployments we support mTLS between customer services and the control plane if you require mutual auth.
[06:58] Sofia: SCIM rate limits — we will provision tens of thousands of users across orgs; need throughput guidance.
[07:04] Riley: SCIM endpoints scale with Dedicated and Private. For hosted we have rate limits per tenant; we can increase for enterprise contracts. For bulk imports we recommend S3-based CSV import or temporary elevated windows.
[07:18] Laura: Auditability of model changes — who changed a model version or routing policy?
[07:24] Ethan: All model and route changes are recorded in the audit log with diff payloads where possible, plus the actor and timestamp. Rollbacks are supported.
[07:34] Raj: For the NDA/procurement piece, legal wants a list of sub-processors and their locations.
[07:40] Maya: We'll send our sub-processor list and data flow diagrams. Those are in the security pack.
[07:46] Tom: If we go private, what is the upgrade window? We have maintenance windows — can upgrades be scheduled?
[07:52] Riley: Yes, Private customers can set maintenance windows and we orchestrate rolling upgrades. For Dedicated we have scheduled maintenance with advance notices.
[07:59] Sofia: A small clarification — how do you map nested SCIM groups into roles if a user is member of parent group and child group with different role mappings? Which takes precedence?
[08:10] Ethan: We evaluate mapped roles deterministically: explicit group-to-role mappings are merged. If there are conflicts we apply deny-overrides if you enable a deny policy; otherwise we union permissions. We'll share exact precedence rules in the mapping doc.
[08:25] Laura: Ok that helps. Any sample SCIM mapping you can share?
[08:28] Ethan: Yes, we'll attach a sample that shows group->role, attribute mappings for department, email, and externalId.
[08:33] Maya: Quick recap before we wrap — action items and owners?
[08:38] Raj: Also want to schedule the follow-up technical session for the private deployment demo.
[08:41] Maya: Noted. We'll aim for week of 12/21.
[08:45] Maya: Thanks everyone. We'll send the docs and schedule.
[08:48] Laura: Thanks all.

Notes: transcription has some minor mishears around product names and times. Shared artifacts mentioned: security pack link (sent after call), SCIM mapping example (to be shared), SOC2 Type II summary, ISO27001 summary, sub-processor list (link).
